title: What Corporate Finance Studies — Fundamentals of Corporate Finance
description: Signature edition. This entry teaches What Corporate Finance Studies as part of the fundamentals of corporate finance, presented the Signature way: from first principles, in plain language, building toward mastery. It sits at the Foundations tier of the teaching ladder, where each idea earns its place before the next is introduced. Signature-authored and Signature-labeled throughout.
overview: In the Signature teaching of corporate finance, What Corporate Finance Studies is a load-bearing idea: understand it and much of the field clicks into place. Time value of money means a dollar today beats a dollar tomorrow, discounted accordingly. Cost of capital means the blended hurdle rate every investment must clear. Together these ideas give the learner working intuition, not just vocabulary. The Signature presentation stresses why each principle holds, shows where it is used in real practice, and connects it forward to the Foundations material that follows.
core_concepts: Time value of money: a dollar today beats a dollar tomorrow, discounted accordingly.
Cost of capital: the blended hurdle rate every investment must clear.
key_laws: NPV rule: accept projects with positive net present value.
vocabulary: WACC: weighted average cost of capital, the hurdle rate.
Leverage: debt amplifying both gains and losses.
methods: DCF modeling: projecting and discounting cash flows rigorously.
history: Corporate finance became quantitative with 1950s-60s breakthroughs: Markowitz, Modigliani-Miller, and Sharpe. DCF and options theory followed, and finance is now the data-driven allocator of corporate capital.
key_points: Time value of money: a dollar today beats a dollar tomorrow, discounted accordingly.
Cost of capital: the blended hurdle rate every investment must clear.
Key vocabulary: WACC — weighted average cost of capital, the hurdle rate.; Leverage — debt amplifying both gains and losses..
Governing principle: NPV rule: accept projects with positive net present value.
how_it_works: The Signature learner approaches What Corporate Finance Studies by anchoring it to what is already known: WACC (weighted average cost of capital, the hurdle rate.), then Leverage (debt amplifying both gains and losses.). The working method is DCF modeling: projecting and discounting cash flows rigorously. Practice means rehearsing the idea until it can be reconstructed from scratch, which is exactly what the accompanying study program drills.
